column1: # THE LABEL OWNERSHIP DECLARATION. Machine-readable on purpose.
# Prose cannot stop the failure this exists for: an agent reads the repo, sees
# a label it thinks should be set, and writes automation that sets it -- while
# a different automation, equally reasonably, withdraws it. Neither is wrong
# about the world. The label has no owner. On PR #9 production:healthy flipped
# five times in twenty minutes between a person and github-actions.
# Before adding ANY label write to ANY script or workflow, find its row here.
# If the writer you are adding is not the declared owner, you are building the
# thrash. gates/label-audit.py enforces this against a PR's timeline.
# owner        the ONE thing that may write this label
# human_add    may a person add it by hand?
# human_rm     may a person remove it by hand?
# persistent   does it survive settlement? PERSISTENT labels describe what the
#              change IS and stay true after it ships. TRANSIENT labels mark where
#              a change sat in the deployment process; once it is merged back to
#              main that position adds no value, so settle.sh clears them. The PR
#              timeline keeps the history either way.
